Copilot's model policy API makes model access a workflow decision.

What changed: on October 19, GitHub made GET and PATCH model-policy endpoints generally available for enterprises, enterprise teams, agent apps and organizations.

What it does: authorized admins can retrieve and update model-availability policies through the API. It manages access; it doesn't choose the best model for your task or prove its output is correct.

Builder value: when a workflow depends on a model, access is part of the build, not an afterthought. Enterprise policies determine where control can be delegated.

On Tech Thursday, we discussed morning roundups and mapping the tasks inside roles. Apply that lesson to the new API: one task, one expected output, one access check before a wider rollout.

Try this week: with an authorized admin, retrieve your org's model policies read-only. Check one model needed for a three-message roundup test. If access is available, run that sample and inspect omissions. Without admin access, ask for confirmation of availability; don't change policy blindly.

The signal: AI is moving beyond prompts into workflows that need explicit operating rules.

Save this for your next AI workflow check.
